articles.summaryZh: 叶澄只有二十分钟带游客看火后的森林。她先选中一处黑色地表，调查组却送来了另外几个地点的照片。
storyParagraphsZh: 森林教育员叶澄要为一条已经重新开放的步道准备二十分钟短课，只能安排很少几个停留点。她原本想在火场边界内选一处黑色地表，告诉游客“这里就是烧过后的样子”，然后把剩下时间留给另一项森林活动。可调查组的资料让这个安排变得太简单了。
在已经获准调查的几个固定点里，一处火前地表燃料较连续，火后低层植被和部分木本变化明显；另一处靠近裸露岩地，燃料分布更断续，资料中保留了更多未烧小斑块；还有一个坡位不同的地点，火后仍能看到存活的木本部分，但地表和低层植物已经发生改变。三处记录旁都附着当时的天气资料，叶澄把它们和照片一一对上。
叶澄把原先的单站课程摊开重排。她不能只挑最黑的一处，因为黑色外观不能告诉游客当时到底释放了多少能量；也不能只挑仍有绿色树冠的一处，因为木本部分存活不代表下面什么都没变。她最终保留三个地点，让大家把火前燃料分布、地形背景和火后留下的生物与地表变化放在一起看，而不是让一个点替整场火说话。
三次短暂停留把原来的时间吃掉了，叶澄只好删去计划中的树皮辨认小游戏。她还把讲义里那张统一涂黑的火场轮廓换成三个地点照片，每到一站只让大家比较眼前还保留什么、什么发生了变化，再和调查记录对应。
正式带队那天，最后一个停留点旁还能看到一块未烧的低矮植被，几步外地表却已经明显改变。计时器震了一下，提醒她二十分钟快到了。叶澄把原本装着树皮卡片的小袋塞回背包，举起三张地点照片，让队伍按刚走过的顺序重新排好。
articles.overallZh: 这篇在讲：同一场火内部可以形成不同的烧过、未烧和生态影响斑块，因为燃料、天气、地形等条件并不处处相同；火后生态影响也不能由外框或颜色一概而论。
explanationParagraphsZh: 相邻的可燃物能让火沿地表继续传播，裸露岩地等缺少可燃物的位置则可能打断这种连续性。燃料数量、含水状态、天气和地形还会共同影响燃烧，因此同一火场内可能留下未烧及生态变化程度不同的斑块。
绿色树冠不说明地表和低层植被没变，黑色地表也不说明所有生物都死亡。
燃烧强度与生态严重度不是同一概念：强度指燃烧过程中能量释放的程度，严重度关注火后生物和环境发生了多大变化。因此不能只凭火后颜色或一张照片倒推完整热释放过程。一次火形成的空间斑块也不等于已经知道该生态系统长期的火情势；后者还涉及频率、季节、范围等长期特征。

moduleZh.intro: 先把一场火的外边界和内部斑块分开，再把燃料、天气和地形等背景与火后生态变化放在一起解释。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么同一场火的三个地点会留下不同的火后结果
diagramSteps: 确定三个地点都处在同一次火的边界内，但火前燃料连续性和地形背景并不完全相同
比较火后资料：有的地点保留未烧小斑块，有的地表和低层植被变化明显，有的仍保留部分木本存活
把这些差异与燃料、天气和地形等可能共同影响燃烧空间表现的因素联系起来
区分燃烧强度与生态严重度，不用黑色程度或绿色树冠单独推断热释放或整体生态影响
把本次火后的斑块作为一次事件的空间结果，并与长期火发生模式分开理解
diagramStepNotes: 同一外框内并不代表燃料、地形或燃烧过程处处相同。
未烧、变化较轻或变化较重都可以在同一火场中形成斑块。
故事只支持这些因素共同影响空间差异的机制，不证明某个单一因素独自造成某一斑块。
强度关注能量释放，严重度关注生物和环境变化，两者不能从单张火后照片互相直接换算。
一次火的斑块分布不是长期火情势本身，不能据此单独推出未来频率、季节或恢复轨迹。
mapping: 燃料较连续的地点 → 燃烧传播条件与其他地点不同的背景之一。
靠裸露岩地的断续燃料 → 可能形成空间中断和未烧小斑块的背景之一。
仍存活的木本部分 → 局部生物存活，不代表地表或全区影响轻微。
黑色地表 → 火后外观，不能直接当成燃烧强度测量。
三个停留点 → 用空间对照代替一个地点代表整场火。
moduleZh.boundary: 本篇只用已开放步道和既有调查资料解释火后生态斑块，不涉及游客进入许可、现场危险判断、点火或规定烧操作。黑色地表不能直接还原燃烧强度，绿色树冠也不能证明生态影响轻微；单次火后观察不能预测恢复结果。一次事件的空间斑块也不能替代长期火情势，后者涉及频率、季节、范围、强度和严重度等更长时间尺度的特征。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果另一次火发生在相似地形上，但当时燃料连续性和天气条件明显不同，你会期待火后斑块一定和这次一样吗？为什么？

referencesZh.citation: National Park Service, Lassen Volcanic National Park. (2022, May 13, updated). Fire Ecology and Effects.
referencesZh.use: 支持火与生物和环境相互作用，同一火场可形成烧过、未烧及不同生态严重度的斑块，并支持区分燃烧强度的能量释放与生态严重度的生物环境变化；本篇不采用特定火间隔，不提供点火或燃烧处方，也不从单张照片判断燃烧强度或安全许可。

referencesZh.citation: National Park Service, Yosemite National Park. (2022, August 17, updated). Fire Ecology and Monitoring.
referencesZh.use: 支持火的作用会随植被、天气和地形而变化，并支持长期火情势包含频率、季节、范围、强度和严重度等特征；本篇不把Yosemite特定林型经验推广到所有生态系统，也不把有火或无火简单写成普遍好坏。

articles.title: One Fire, Three Stops
articles.summary: Ye Cheng has twenty minutes to show visitors a forest after fire. She chooses a patch of blackened ground, then the survey team sends photographs from other locations.
storyParagraphs: Forest educator Ye Cheng has to prepare a twenty-minute lesson for a trail that has already reopened, leaving room for only a few stops. She originally plans to choose one patch of blackened ground within the fire perimeter, tell visitors, “This is what it looks like after a fire,” and save the remaining time for another forest activity. But the survey team's records make that arrangement look too simple.

Among several fixed points already included in authorized survey work, one location had relatively continuous surface fuel before the fire and later showed marked changes in low vegetation and some woody plants. Another lies beside exposed rock, where fuel distribution was more discontinuous and the records retain more small unburned patches. At a third point with a different slope position, surviving woody parts can still be seen after the fire even though the ground surface and low vegetation have changed. The records include the weather at the time. Ye Cheng matches each sheet to its site photograph.

Ye Cheng spreads out her original one-stop lesson and rearranges it. She cannot choose only the blackest location, because black appearance cannot tell visitors how much energy was released during burning. Nor can she choose only a place with surviving green canopy, because survival of woody parts does not mean nothing changed below. She keeps all three locations so that visitors can compare pre-fire fuel distribution, topographic context, and the biological and surface changes left after the fire rather than letting one point speak for the entire event.

Three short stops consume the time she had set aside, so Ye Cheng removes the planned bark-identification game. She also replaces the uniformly blackened fire-perimeter outline in the handout with three site photographs. At each stop, she asks visitors first to compare what remains and what has changed around them, then to relate those observations to the survey records.

On the day of the walk, a patch of low vegetation remains unburned beside the final stop, while only a few steps away the ground surface is visibly altered. The timer vibrates to warn her that the twenty minutes are nearly over. Ye Cheng puts the unused bag of bark cards back into her backpack, raises the three site photographs, and asks the group to arrange them in the order of the locations they have just visited.
articles.overall: This article explains that a single fire can contain burned, unburned, and differently affected ecological patches because fuel, weather, topography, and other conditions are not uniform across the area; post-fire ecological effects therefore cannot be inferred from the perimeter or surface colour alone.
explanationParagraphs: Adjacent combustible material can allow fire to keep spreading along the ground, while gaps in that material, such as exposed rock, can interrupt local continuity. Fuel amount and moisture, weather, and terrain also influence burning, so one fire can leave unburned patches and patches with different ecological effects.
A green canopy does not mean the ground and low vegetation were unchanged; blackened ground does not mean every organism died.

Fire intensity and ecological severity are not the same concept. Intensity concerns the degree of energy release during burning, while severity concerns how much biological and environmental change occurred after the fire. Post-fire colour or a single photograph therefore cannot reconstruct the full energy-release process. The spatial patchiness produced by one fire also does not by itself establish the ecosystem's long-term fire regime, which involves longer-term characteristics such as frequency, season, and extent.

module.intro: Separate the outer perimeter of one fire from the patches within it, then interpret post-fire ecological change alongside background differences in fuel, weather, and topography.
module.diagramTitle: Why Did Three Locations Within the Same Fire Leave Different Post-Fire Outcomes?
diagramSteps: Establish that all three locations lie within the same fire perimeter while their pre-fire fuel continuity and topographic settings are not identical
Compare the post-fire records: some locations retain small unburned patches, some show marked changes in ground surface and low vegetation, and some retain surviving woody parts
Relate these differences to factors such as fuel, weather, and topography that can jointly influence the spatial expression of fire
Distinguish fire intensity from ecological severity, and do not use the darkness of the ground or the presence of green canopy alone to infer heat release or overall ecological impact
Treat the post-fire patches as spatial outcomes of one event and keep them conceptually separate from the long-term pattern of fire occurrence
diagramStepNotes: Being inside the same perimeter does not mean fuel, topography, or the burning process was identical everywhere.
Unburned, less changed, and more strongly changed patches can all occur within the same fire area.
The story supports only the mechanism that these factors can jointly influence spatial differences; it does not prove that any one factor alone created a particular patch.
Intensity concerns energy release, while severity concerns biological and environmental change; neither can be directly converted into the other from a single post-fire photograph.
The patch pattern from one fire is not itself the long-term fire regime and cannot by itself establish future frequency, season, or recovery trajectory.
mapping: Location with more continuous fuel → one background condition in which fire spread conditions differ from other sites.
Discontinuous fuel beside exposed rock → one background condition that can contribute to spatial interruption and small unburned patches.
Surviving woody parts → local biological survival, not proof that ground-level or whole-area impacts were minor.
Blackened ground → a post-fire appearance, not a direct measurement of fire intensity.
Three lesson stops → using spatial comparison instead of allowing one location to represent the entire fire.
module.boundary: This article uses an already reopened trail and existing survey records only to interpret post-fire ecological patchiness; it does not address visitor-entry authorization, on-site hazard assessment, ignition, or prescribed burning operations. Blackened ground cannot directly reconstruct fire intensity, and green canopy does not prove that ecological effects were minor. A single post-fire observation cannot predict recovery. Spatial patches from one event also cannot substitute for a long-term fire regime, which includes characteristics such as frequency, season, extent, intensity, and severity over longer time scales.
module.reflection: If another fire occurred on similar terrain but fuel continuity and weather conditions were substantially different, would you expect its post-fire patch pattern to be identical to this one? Why or why not?

references.citation: National Park Service, Lassen Volcanic National Park. (2022, May 13, updated). Fire Ecology and Effects.
references.use: Supports that fire interacts with living organisms and the environment, that a single fire area can contain burned, unburned, and differently severe ecological patches, and that fire intensity as energy release differs from ecological severity as biological and environmental change. This article does not adopt any specific fire-return interval, provide ignition or burning prescriptions, or use a single post-fire photograph to determine fire intensity or access authorization.

references.citation: National Park Service, Yosemite National Park. (2022, August 17, updated). Fire Ecology and Monitoring.
references.use: Supports that fire effects vary with vegetation, weather, and topography and that long-term fire regimes include characteristics such as frequency, season, extent, intensity, and severity. This article does not generalize experience from specific Yosemite forest types to all ecosystems and does not portray the presence or absence of fire as universally good or bad.

articles.summaryZh: 午前就要回复冷库了。唐沅想拿整排仓位的折扣，却还不能确定合作社下一季的稳定到货量。
storyParagraphsZh: 渔业合作社必须在中午前回复冷库：是整季锁下一整排仓位，还是按月订较灵活的小批仓位。整排方案更便宜，但要求唐沅提前给出较稳定的到货承诺。她负责协调合作社的供货和仓储，原本觉得科学人员既然已经解释过一个“长期捕量参照”，就足以支撑他们把仓位订得更固定一些。
唐沅给科学人员打了电话。对方没有给她一个可直接填进订单的鱼货数字，而是重新打开那张教学增长图：在简化模型里，三个独立的种群状态分别是生物量20、50和80个单位，对应的瞬时净增加速度分别是16、25和16个单位每教学时间单位。25描述的是模型在特定状态下的增长峰值，不是合作社下一季必然拥有的鱼货。
她这才发现自己缺的不是一个更漂亮的峰值，而是现实种群此刻处在哪个状态、环境条件有没有变化，以及评估本身有多大不确定性。唐沅能决定的是冷库怎么订，不能替有权限的管理程序设定捕捞许可或年度限制。她把原来准备支持整季固定仓位的内部建议撤回，改选按月调整的方案。
冷库经理在电话里确认：“那整排折扣就不要了？”唐沅答应下来。灵活方案价格更高，旺季也可能拿不到最方便的库位，于是她同时在合作社自己的排程里留出临时转运余量。科学图仍留在内部资料里，只作为理解增长与移除关系的参照。
中午前，新预约单传回冷库。原来整排锁仓的位置改成了按月更新的栏位，旁边多了一行灵活仓储附加费。唐沅签完字，把增长图放回资源评估资料夹，将预约单发给冷库经理。
articles.overallZh: 最大可持续产量是在给定环境和模型条件下可长期支持的最大平均捕量参照。现实当期能承受多少捕捞，还取决于当前种群状态和不确定性；模型参照不能直接代替年度限制或商业到货承诺。
explanationParagraphsZh: 在此简化模型中，生物量很少时总增长受基数小的限制；接近环境上限时，资源限制又压低净增加速度。B表示生物量，承载量K=100单位，低密度每单位生物量的净增长参数r=1/教学时间单位。
无捕捞时瞬时净增长率G(B)=rB(1-B/K)。三个独立状态B=20、50、80，对应G=16、25、16个生物量单位每教学时间单位，并非连续三年或上岸量。模型可写成G(B)=25-(B-50)^2/100，所以在0≤B≤100内，B=50时增长率最高为25。
只有在这个定参、无迁移的连续时间模型中，生物量维持在50、持续移除率恰与净增长率相等，25才对应模型内可维持的最大捕获率。这不是从三个点直接推出实际年配额。
现实MSY是在给定条件下可长期支持的最大平均捕量参照。年度限制还需当前种群状态、环境、补充与不确定性信息，通常需要缓冲；参照本身不能保证下一季固定到货。

moduleZh.intro: 把模型中的长期增长参照与现实年度捕捞控制分开：先理解增长如何随种群状态变化，再检查现实状态和不确定性是否足以支持具体管理决定。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么模型里的增长峰值25不能直接变成下一季固定鱼货承诺
diagramSteps: 先说明模型如何把种群生物量与净增加速度联系起来，再设K=100、r=1并写出G(B)
分别代入三个独立种群状态B=20、50、80，得到瞬时净增长率16、25、16单位每教学时间单位
将模型改写为G(B)=25-(B-50)^2/100，确认仅在该模型内部B=50时峰值为25
在此定参模型内，只有种群维持相应状态、持续移除与净增长相等时，增长参照才对应可维持的捕获率
在现实年度控制前继续使用当前种群监测、环境信息和不确定性，并由有权限的管理程序设置适当限制与缓冲
diagramStepNotes: K和r都是本教学模型的设定，不是某个真实鱼群的测量结果。
20、50、80是三个独立状态，不是连续三年的种群变化轨迹。
三个示例点本身不足以证明全局峰值；峰值来自完整模型关系及其代数形式。
增长率25的单位是生物量单位每教学时间单位，不是一步后的种群数量、上岸量或年度配额。
模型或环境条件变化时，参照也可能改变；年度控制需要监测和不确定性缓冲。
mapping: 整排固定仓位 → 需要较稳定商业到货承诺的仓储选择。
按月灵活仓位 → 唐沅在缺少足够现实资源信息时选择的可调整商业安排。
B=20/50/80 → 简化模型中的三个独立种群状态。
16/25/16 → 各状态下的瞬时净增长率，不是现实鱼货数量。
管理程序 → 有权根据现实评估与不确定性设置年度捕捞控制的主体，而不是合作社仓储协调人。
moduleZh.boundary: 最大可持续产量并不是所有物种都在某个简单‘中等种群’状态达到固定峰值的自然定律。本篇K=100、r=1以及16/25/16均为虚构纸面模型数字。年龄结构、环境条件、补充过程、观测误差和执行误差都会影响现实结论；旧模型或环境变化时参照需要更新。稳定上岸量也不能单独证明种群稳定。本篇不提供真实配额、捕捞许可或特定司法管辖区的管理程序。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果环境变化使模型承载量不再是100，你还会沿用原来的50和25吗？重新考虑参照与下一季承诺时，需要更新哪些信息？

referencesZh.citation: Fisheries and Oceans Canada. (2026, January 7). Introduction to stock assessment: Unit 1.3, Stock status and reference points.
referencesZh.use: 支持把MSY理解为给定条件下种群可长期支持的最大平均产量参照，并结合B_MSY等种群状态参照及不确定性解释；本篇的K=100、r=1和16/25/16均为虚构教学模型，不取自该页面，也不采用页面示例警戒比例作为通用阈值。

referencesZh.citation: NOAA Fisheries. (n.d.). Setting an Annual Catch Limit.
referencesZh.use: 支持区分MSY等长期参照与实际年度捕捞限制，并说明科学不确定性、管理不确定性和缓冲会进入年度控制；本篇只借用‘参照不等于操作承诺’的逻辑，不把美国程序描述成世界统一的法定做法。

articles.title: A Storage Booking Before Noon
articles.summary: Tang Yuan must reply to the cold-storage operator before noon. She wants the full-row discount, but the cooperative’s steady arrival volume for next season is still uncertain.
storyParagraphs: The fisheries cooperative has to reply to the cold-storage operator before noon: either lock in a full row of storage for the entire season or reserve smaller, more flexible amounts month by month. The full-row option is cheaper, but it requires Tang Yuan to give a relatively stable arrival commitment in advance. She coordinates the cooperative's supply and storage and initially thinks that, since the scientists have already explained a 'long-term catch reference', that should be enough to justify making the storage reservation more fixed.

Tang Yuan calls the scientist. Instead of giving her a fish quantity that can be entered directly into the order, the scientist reopens the teaching growth graph. In the simplified model, three independent stock states have biomasses of 20, 50, and 80 units, with corresponding instantaneous rates of net increase of 16, 25, and 16 biomass units per teaching-time unit. The 25 describes the growth peak under a particular state in the model; it is not fish that the cooperative is guaranteed to have next season.

She realizes that what she is missing is not a more attractive peak value but information about the stock's actual current state, whether environmental conditions have changed, and how uncertain the assessment is. Tang Yuan can decide how to reserve cold storage, but she cannot set harvesting permits or annual catch controls on behalf of the authorized management process. She withdraws her internal recommendation to reserve fixed full-season space and chooses the month-by-month adjustable option instead.

The cold-storage manager confirms over the phone: “So you don't want the full-row discount?” Tang Yuan agrees. The flexible option costs more, and during the busiest period they may not get the most convenient storage location, so she also leaves room in the cooperative's own schedule for temporary transfers. The scientific graph remains in the internal file only as a reference for understanding the relationship between stock growth and removals.

Before noon, the revised reservation form reaches the cold-storage operator. The fixed full-row booking has become a set of monthly update fields, with an extra line for the flexible-storage surcharge. Tang Yuan signs it, returns the growth graph to the resource-assessment file, and sends the reservation to the cold-storage manager.
articles.overall: Maximum sustainable yield is a reference for the largest average catch that can be supported over the long term under specified environmental and model conditions. What a stock can support now also depends on its current state and uncertainty; the reference cannot replace an annual limit or a commercial arrival commitment.
explanationParagraphs: In this simplified model, low biomass limits total growth through a small starting base; near carrying capacity, resource limits reduce net increase. B denotes biomass, K=100 biomass units is carrying capacity, and r=1 per teaching-time unit is the low-density net growth parameter per unit of biomass.

Without fishing, instantaneous net growth is G(B)=rB(1-B/K). Independent states B=20, 50, 80 give G=16, 25, 16 biomass units per teaching-time unit, not successive years or landed catch. Since G(B)=25-(B-50)^2/100, within 0≤B≤100 the peak is 25 at B=50.

Only in this fixed-parameter, no-migration, continuous-time model, with biomass maintained at 50 and ongoing removal exactly matching net growth, does 25 correspond to the maximum sustainable model catch rate. Three sample points do not establish a real annual quota.

Real MSY is a reference for the largest average catch supportable over time under specified conditions. Annual limits still require current stock status, environmental and recruitment information, uncertainty, and typically a buffer. The reference alone cannot guarantee next season’s arrivals.

module.intro: Keep the model's long-run growth reference separate from real annual catch control: first understand how growth changes with stock state, then ask whether real stock information and uncertainty are sufficient to support a specific management decision.
module.diagramTitle: Why Can't a Model Growth Peak of 25 Be Turned Directly into a Fixed Fish-Supply Commitment for Next Season?
diagramSteps: First explain how the model links biomass to net increase, then set K=100 and r=1 and write G(B)
Substitute three independent stock states B=20, 50, and 80 to obtain instantaneous net growth rates of 16, 25, and 16 biomass units per teaching-time unit
Rewrite the model as G(B)=25-(B-50)^2/100 to confirm that only within this model the peak is 25 at B=50
Within this fixed-parameter model, a growth reference corresponds to a maintainable catch rate only when the stock is kept at that state and ongoing removal equals net growth
Before setting real annual controls, continue using current stock monitoring, environmental information, and uncertainty, with appropriate limits and buffers set by the authorized management process
diagramStepNotes: K and r are settings of this teaching model, not measurements from a real fish stock.
20, 50, and 80 are three independent states, not a three-year sequence of stock change.
The three sample points alone are insufficient to prove the global peak; the peak follows from the full model relationship and its algebraic form.
The unit of the growth rate 25 is biomass units per teaching-time unit, not stock quantity after one step, landed catch, or an annual quota.
If model conditions or environmental conditions change, the reference may also change; annual control requires monitoring and buffers for uncertainty.
mapping: Fixed full-row cold storage → a storage choice that requires a relatively stable commercial arrival commitment.
Flexible monthly storage → the adjustable commercial arrangement Tang Yuan chooses when real resource information is insufficient for a fixed commitment.
B=20/50/80 → three independent stock states in the simplified model.
16/25/16 → instantaneous rates of net growth at those states, not real fish quantities.
Authorized management process → the body that sets annual catch controls using real assessment and uncertainty, rather than the cooperative's storage coordinator.
module.boundary: Maximum sustainable yield is not a natural law stating that every species reaches a fixed growth peak at some simple 'middle' stock size. The values K=100, r=1, and 16/25/16 in this article are fictional teaching-model values. Age structure, environmental conditions, recruitment, observation error, and implementation error can all affect real conclusions, and references need updating when models or environmental conditions change. Stable landings alone also do not prove that a stock is stable. This article provides no real quota, harvesting permit, or management procedure for any specific jurisdiction.
module.reflection: If environmental change means the model’s carrying capacity is no longer 100, would you retain the old 50 and 25? Which information would need updating before reconsidering the reference and next season’s commitment?

references.citation: Fisheries and Oceans Canada. (2026, January 7). Introduction to stock assessment: Unit 1.3, Stock status and reference points.
references.use: Supports understanding MSY as the maximum average yield a stock can sustain over the long term under specified conditions, interpreted together with stock-status reference points such as B_MSY and uncertainty. The values K=100, r=1, and 16/25/16 in this article are fictional teaching-model values, not data from the page, and the page's example cautionary proportions are not used as universal thresholds.

references.citation: NOAA Fisheries. (n.d.). Setting an Annual Catch Limit.
references.use: Supports distinguishing long-term references such as MSY from actual annual catch limits and recognizes that scientific uncertainty, management uncertainty, and buffers enter annual control. This article borrows only the logic that a reference is not the same as an operational commitment and does not present the U.S. process as a universal legal procedure.

articles.summaryZh: 餐厅们等着确定下一季度的食材成本。孟青手里的两份鱼货记录，目标鱼到货量差不多，附件却不一样。
storyParagraphsZh: 海边几家餐厅已经把下一季度的菜单排好，只等采购合作社锁定鱼货供应。孟青负责在两家长期供货方之间做选择：两边记录里的目标鱼上岸量相近，其中一家价格明显更低。厨师们等着固定成本，她也已经把那份便宜的季度合同放到了签字夹最上面。
下午，她在另一家供应记录的附件里看到了一页平时很少进入菜单会议的内容：作业过程中还有一些没有作为目标鱼上岸销售的生物，其中一部分被弃回，而这些弃回个体中有些后续情况无法确认。记录旁还注明，有些非目标生物也是其他动物的食物，还有一些属于别的渔民赖以谋生的种群。孟青第一次发现，餐厅最终收到多少目标鱼，只描述了捕捞活动的一部分。
她又翻回价格更低的那份记录，弃获一栏只有零散备注。两边到底有多大差别，还比不出来。另一份资料里，一尾非目标鱼放回时仍能游动，之后是否存活却不知道。孟青在这一行旁边贴上“未知”，没有把空格填成零。
孟青把季度合同收回签字夹，先让合作社延长一小段现有采购安排，同时请两边用可比较的方式补充能提供的弃获和后续信息。当天主厨来问下一季价格，她只能先给出更贵的短期报价。菜单已经排好，固定成本却还得再等等。
第二天早上，主厨们来开菜单会。桌上仍摆着两份目标鱼到货记录，旁边多了一张画着简单食物关系箭头的便签和几处标着“未知”的黄色标签。有人把季度合同推到孟青面前，她没有拿笔，而是先把那张便签压在合同签字栏上，请大家把没进餐厅箱子的那部分也看完。
articles.overallZh: 这篇在讲：目标渔获上岸量只描述捕捞影响的一部分；未上岸的非目标生物仍可能受伤或死亡，并与其他物种、栖息地和人的利用关系相连，因此不能把未知或弃回自动记成零影响。
explanationParagraphsZh: 捕捞活动除了目标渔获，还可能捕到非目标生物，其中一部分会被弃回。释放时还能游动并不能证明最终存活，因为之后仍可能受到受伤、应激或捕食等影响。
如果后续结果未知，合理做法是保留未知，而不是填成零死亡或自行编出死亡率。
未上岸生物仍可能属于其他种群、参与食物关系，或与其他渔业和栖息地相联系，因此只看目标鱼上岸量不足以描述全部影响。但一份记录更完整也不等于对应供应方实际影响一定更小，记录不足也不证明另一方更差。把这些信息纳入判断只是生态系统视角的一个入口，不等于完成了完整的生态系统渔业管理。

moduleZh.intro: 把‘卖上岸的目标鱼’和‘捕捞过程中还影响了什么’分开，再把未知的释放后结果保留为未知。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么两家目标鱼上岸量相近，仍不足以说明捕捞影响相近
diagramSteps: 先比较两家相近的目标鱼上岸记录，确认这只描述进入销售链的目标渔获
再查看是否存在被捕获但未作为目标鱼上岸销售的非目标生物和弃回记录
对释放个体区分‘释放时仍活着’与‘最终存活’，缺少后续信息时保留未知
考虑非目标生物被移除或受伤死亡后，可能怎样影响以它们为食的动物、相关种群和其他渔民的生计
据此把采购或管理判断从单一上岸量扩展到更多影响信息，但不把一次记录扩充当成完整生态系统管理
diagramStepNotes: 目标鱼上岸量不能代表捕捞过程中所有生物影响。
不同制度对兼捕和保留非目标渔获的术语可能不同，本篇聚焦未上岸弃获及其影响。
释放时游动只是当下状态，不等于之后一定存活；未知既不能记零，也不能自行编死亡数。
生态关系意味着未售出的生物仍可能影响或受到其他种群和人类利用的联系，但不能据此把某一鱼群变化全部归因于兼捕。
一次记录变得更完整只是让判断信息增加，不等于已经建立完整生态系统模型或现实捕捞处方。
mapping: 相近的目标鱼到货记录 → 两家在销售端看起来相似的部分。
未上岸的非目标生物 → 原本没有进入餐厅采购比较的捕捞影响。
释放时仍能游动 → 当下观察，不能替代最终存活信息。
黄色‘未知’标签 → 不把缺失信息自动当作零影响。
食物关系便签 → 提醒未上岸生物仍属于更广的生态和人类利用关系。
moduleZh.boundary: 本篇不根据两份商业记录判断哪一家真实生态影响更大，也不把记录缺失当作实际兼捕更严重。目标渔获变化可能同时受环境、捕捞努力和种群状态等因素影响，不能把任何种群衰退全部归因于一艘船或一种兼捕关系。释放时活着不保证最终存活，未知不能填零或虚构死亡率。把弃获、生态关系和人的取舍纳入判断只是生态系统渔业视角的一部分，不提供现实配额、放流操作或法域法律结论。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果两家供应方后来都提供了同样完整的弃获记录，但其中一种非目标生物在当地食物关系和其他渔业中的作用明显不同，你还会只比较弃获数量吗？为什么？

referencesZh.citation: NOAA Fisheries. (n.d.). Understanding Bycatch.
referencesZh.use: 支持非目标与弃获生物可能受伤或死亡，并可能影响非目标种群、食物关系和栖息地，也支持通过观察和记录帮助评估这些影响；本篇聚焦未上岸弃获及其生态意义，不宣称各法域对所有非目标渔获采用完全相同的术语或定义。

referencesZh.citation: NOAA Fisheries, Office of Science and Technology. (2019, April 3, updated). Fish Discard and Release Mortality Science.
referencesZh.use: 支持释放时仍活着的鱼之后仍可能因受伤、应激或捕食等原因死亡，并支持改进释放后死亡估计并纳入评估；本篇不凭单次游走观察确认最终存活，不把未知当作零，也不提供现实放流操作。

referencesZh.citation: NOAA Fisheries, Office of Science and Technology. (2024, November 27, updated). Ecosystem-Based Fisheries Management.
referencesZh.use: 支持渔业判断需要考虑物种相互作用、环境与栖息地、人类活动、多重压力及其取舍；本篇只借用这一更广视角说明为什么目标上岸量不足以代表全部影响，不把一次记录扩充写成完整生态系统模型，也不据此给出现实配额或唯一归因。

articles.title: The Note on the Signature Line
articles.summary: The restaurants are waiting to fix next quarter's ingredient costs. Meng Qing has two fish-supply records with similar target-fish deliveries but different supporting information.
storyParagraphs: Several seaside restaurants have already planned their menus for the next quarter and are waiting only for their purchasing cooperative to secure the fish supply. Meng Qing is responsible for choosing between two long-term suppliers. Their records show similar landed quantities of the target fish, while one supplier offers a clearly lower price. The chefs are waiting for fixed costs, and she has already placed the cheaper quarterly contract at the top of the signature folder.

That afternoon, she finds a page in the other supplier's supporting records that rarely appears in menu meetings. During fishing operations, other organisms had also been caught without being landed and sold as the target fish; some were discarded, and the later outcomes of some of those discarded animals could not be confirmed. The notes also indicate that some non-target organisms are food for other animals, while others belong to populations on which other fishers depend for their livelihoods. Meng Qing realizes for the first time that the amount of target fish eventually received by the restaurants describes only part of the fishing activity.

She turns back to the cheaper supplier's record. The discard column holds only scattered notes; she cannot yet tell how the two suppliers' impacts compare. In the other file, one non-target fish was still swimming at release, but its later survival is unknown. Meng Qing puts an “unknown” label beside that entry and leaves the blank without a zero.

Meng Qing returns the quarterly contract to the folder. She arranges a short extension of the existing supply and asks both suppliers for comparable discard and follow-up information where available. When a chef calls that day to ask about next season's price, she can offer only the more expensive short-term quote. The menus are ready; the fixed costs will have to wait.

The next morning, the chefs arrive for the menu meeting. The two target-fish delivery records are still on the table, now beside a note with a simple food-web arrow and several yellow labels marked “unknown.” Someone pushes the quarterly contract toward Meng Qing. She does not pick up the pen. Instead, she places the note over the signature line and asks everyone to finish looking at the part that never entered the restaurant boxes.
articles.overall: This article explains that landed target catch describes only part of fishing impacts. Non-target organisms that are not landed can still be injured or die and can remain connected to other species, habitats, and human uses, so unknown outcomes or discarded organisms cannot automatically be counted as zero impact.
explanationParagraphs: Fishing can catch non-target organisms in addition to the target catch, and some of these organisms may be discarded. Being able to swim at the time of release does not prove eventual survival, because injury, stress, predation, or other effects may still lead to later mortality.
When the later outcome is unknown, the appropriate representation is to retain that uncertainty rather than record zero mortality or invent a mortality rate.

Organisms that are not landed may still belong to other populations, participate in food-web relationships, or connect to other fisheries and habitats, so target-fish landings alone cannot describe the full set of impacts. But more complete records do not mean that the corresponding supplier necessarily had lower actual impacts, and missing records do not prove that another supplier was worse. Bringing this information into a decision is only one entry point into an ecosystem perspective, not a complete implementation of ecosystem-based fisheries management.

module.intro: Separate 'target fish sold after landing' from 'what else was affected during fishing,' and preserve unknown post-release outcomes as unknown.
module.diagramTitle: Why Are Similar Target-Fish Landings Still Not Enough to Show Similar Fishing Impacts?
diagramSteps: First compare the two suppliers' similar target-fish landing records and recognize that these describe only the target catch entering the sales chain
Then check whether non-target organisms were caught but not landed and sold as target fish, including any discard records
For released organisms, distinguish 'alive at release' from 'eventual survival' and retain unknown outcomes when follow-up information is missing
Consider how removal, injury, or death of non-target organisms could affect animals that eat them, related populations, and other fishers' livelihoods
Use that broader information to expand purchasing or management judgment beyond landing quantity alone without treating one improvement in records as complete ecosystem management
diagramStepNotes: Target-fish landings do not represent every biological effect of fishing activity.
Terminology for bycatch and retained non-target catch can vary across management systems; this article focuses on discarded organisms that were not landed and their impacts.

Swimming at release is only an immediate condition and does not mean the organism definitely survives afterward; unknown outcomes cannot be recorded as zero or replaced by an invented mortality number.

Ecological relationships mean that organisms not sold can still affect or be connected to other populations and human uses, but this does not prove that all change in a particular stock was caused by bycatch.
More complete records increase the information available for judgment; they do not by themselves constitute a complete ecosystem model or a real-world fishing prescription.
mapping: Similar target-fish delivery records → the part of the two suppliers that looks similar at the sales end.
Non-target organisms that were not landed → fishing impacts that had originally been absent from the restaurant purchasing comparison.
Still able to swim at release → an immediate observation that cannot replace information about eventual survival.
Yellow 'unknown' labels → preserving missing information rather than automatically treating it as zero impact.
Food-web note → a reminder that organisms that never reach the market still belong to wider ecological and human-use relationships.
module.boundary: This article does not use the two commercial records to determine which supplier has the larger real ecological impact, and it does not treat missing records as evidence of more severe actual bycatch. Changes in target catch or stock condition may also be influenced by the environment, fishing effort, stock dynamics, and other factors, so decline in a population cannot be attributed entirely to one vessel or one bycatch relationship. Being alive at release does not guarantee eventual survival, and unknown outcomes must not be recorded as zero or assigned an invented mortality rate. Bringing discards, ecological relationships, and human trade-offs into judgment is only one part of an ecosystem-based fisheries perspective and does not provide real quotas, release procedures, or jurisdiction-specific legal conclusions.
module.reflection: If both suppliers later provided equally complete discard records, but one non-target species played a clearly different role in the local food web and in other fisheries, would you still compare only the number discarded? Why or why not?

references.citation: NOAA Fisheries. (n.d.). Understanding Bycatch.
references.use: Supports that non-target and discarded organisms can be injured or die and can affect non-target populations, food-web relationships, and habitat, and supports the use of observation and records to help assess these effects. This article focuses on the ecological significance of discarded organisms that are not landed and does not claim that every jurisdiction uses identical terminology or definitions for all non-target catch.

references.use: Supports that fish released alive can still die later because of injury, stress, predation, or related causes and supports improving estimates of post-release mortality and incorporating them into assessment. This article does not use a single observation of a fish swimming away to confirm eventual survival, does not treat unknown outcomes as zero, and provides no real-world release procedure.

references.use: Supports considering species interactions, environment and habitat, human activities, multiple pressures, and their trade-offs in fisheries decisions. This article borrows only that broader perspective to explain why target landings are insufficient to represent all impacts, does not treat one expansion of record-keeping as a complete ecosystem model, and does not use it to provide a real quota or a single-cause attribution.

articles.summaryZh: 程放想在周五前定好一条渔业作业边界。办公室里的直线很省事，渔民带来的几张透明纸却让它不再那么简单。
storyParagraphsZh: 渔港管理站准备试行一条临时作业边界，把一小片水域里的定置网作业和流动作业尽量分开，看看两类作业反复挤到同一处的情况能不能减少。程放负责在周五前把线定下来。办公室已经画好一版：沿着图上最直的方向切过去，标记少，之后巡查看图也方便。
第一次看图时，两类作业的人都来了。长期布设定置网的使用者把不同潮位下常用的网位画在透明纸上，做流动作业的人则标出常用作业水面。几张纸叠起来后，程放发现，原直线会把一段常用网位排出定置网可用区域；如果这些作业转到试行分区外的相邻水面，就可能与那里已有的流动作业重新重叠。图内分开了，问题却可能被挤到图外。
两边也没有同一个答案。定置网一方希望保留一段长期使用的位置，流动作业一方则担心那会让可用水面变窄。按原先做法，程放完全可以听完意见后由管理站自己选一个折中方案；但这项试行的授权文件本来就允许管理站把这一个边界位置与两类作业代表共同确定。程放于是把三个可选方案并排摊开，管理人员和两类受影响代表一起删掉不能接受的版本，最后共同定下一条。
管理站要把共同定下的边界正式发出，再汇总记录、安排复看。两类作业代表也分好任务，记下重叠、异常和各自使用位置的变化，到时一起解释记录。管理站得重做一套试行图，几位代表则把原定离港的下午留给了记录方法的核对。墙上的钟走过了原本散会的时间，三张方案纸还铺在桌上。
周五下午，新图被铺在码头仓库的木桌上。程放拿起原来的直线稿，和新图比了几秒，最后把旧稿卷起来塞进图筒。桌边那支用了半截的铅笔还压着新边界，旁边空出一小块位置，留给下一次复看时继续画。
articles.overallZh: 这篇在讲一种共同决策形式：资源使用者在明确授权范围内与公共机构共同选择管理安排，并承担相应的记录和复核责任，参与因此不止于提供意见。
explanationParagraphsZh: 本例把共同决定限制在一个很窄的管理事项：定置网与流动作业之间的临时作业边界。管理站原本拥有决定权，但既有授权允许把这个边界选择与两类受影响使用者共同决定，因此使用者提供的信息不仅进入记录，还实际改变了可选方案和最终边界。
本例选的是共同作出这一决定的合作形式；现实共同管理还包括不同程度的咨询、合作或委托安排，不能把本例当成唯一合法模板。
共同管理并不要求各方拥有完全相同的权力，也不表示公共机构退出。管理站仍承担正式发布、汇总和复核责任，使用者则承担约定的观察、记录和解释责任。一次共同决定也不能证明作业冲突、资源状况或生态结果已经改善，后续仍需要实际记录和复看。

moduleZh.intro: 本例关注共同作出决定的合作形式：在一个明确授权的事项上分享选择，并让后续责任与之相配。现实共同管理还有其他权责分配形式。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么提供作业数据还不等于共同管理
diagramSteps: 管理站先明确试行事项：只决定定置网与流动作业之间的一条临时作业边界
两类受影响作业代表提供各自实际使用位置，使原先直线方案暴露出新的重叠问题
依据既有授权，管理站不再独自决定，而是让管理人员与两类代表共同从可选边界中作出选择
最终边界确定后，管理站保留正式发布和汇总职责，两类代表承担约定的使用记录和异常说明责任
到复看时间，各方用共同收集和解释的信息重新评估这条边界是否需要维持或调整
diagramStepNotes: 具体管理对象必须明确；本例讨论的是两类作业安排，不是通航权、配额或整个渔业治理体系。
地方经验显示原分区可能把作业挤到相邻水面；这仍需实际记录检验。收集意见和数据本身不能证明已经分享了本例的共同决定权。
共享权力可以是不均等的；关键是使用者在授权范围内确实能影响决定，而不是只旁听结果。
权力与责任需要相配：谁参与选择，也需要承担与该范围相符的实施、记录或复核责任。
一次共同选择只是一个治理安排，不能单凭会议或新边界宣称冲突、渔获或生态状况已经改善。
mapping: 三条可选边界 → 授权范围内真正可以共同决定的管理选项。
定置网代表与流动作业代表 → 两类直接受该边界影响的资源使用者。
透明纸上的实际作业位置 → 地方使用经验进入管理判断的证据。
管理站正式发布与汇总 → 公共机构仍保留的职责。
下一次共同复看 → 决定、实施、记录与评估形成连续责任链。
moduleZh.boundary: 本篇只展示一个已存在授权下的局部共同管理环节，不说明现实法域中的具体法权、配额或许可安排。共享权力不必均等，各方能力和责任也可能不同；仅参加会议、提供数据或听取汇报并不自动构成共同管理。地方经验和调查资料都需要检验，任何单一代表也不能自动代表所有受影响者。一次共同决定不保证冲突、渔获或生态状况改善，也不把作业边界解释为禁航线。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果管理站仍让两类作业者记录数据、参加每次讨论，却规定最终边界只能由管理站在会后独自选择，这和故事里的安排相比，真正少了哪一部分？

referencesZh.citation: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. (n.d.). Report of the Expert Consultation on Small-Scale Fisheries Management in Sub-Saharan Africa, Accra, Ghana, 12–14 December 2001: Co-management.
referencesZh.use: 支持资源使用者与公共机构等在界定范围内分享管理责任与权力，并支持共同管理可以有多种安排而不等于政府放弃责任；本篇只借用这一一般治理关系，不把地区经验泛化到所有渔业，不提供现实法权或配额，也不保证一次共同决定带来资源恢复。

referencesZh.citation: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. (n.d.). Guidelines for designing data collection and sharing systems for co-managed fisheries. Part 2: Technical guidelines. Section 2: The information needs of co-managers.
referencesZh.use: 支持共同管理中的角色、数据收集与解释、决策实施和评估职责需要相互匹配，并支持不同伙伴和问题尺度下的分享安排并非固定比例；本篇只展示一个授权边界决定，明确协助采数本身不等于获得完整管理权。

articles.title: The Boundary on the Transparent Sheets
articles.summary: Cheng Fang wants a fishing boundary settled by Friday. The office's straight line is convenient, until fishers lay their transparent sheets over it.
storyParagraphs: The fishing port management office is preparing to trial a temporary operating boundary intended to separate set-net operations and mobile fishing operations in a small area of water and see whether repeated overlap between the two can be reduced. Cheng Fang is responsible for fixing the line by Friday. The office has already drawn one version: it cuts across the chart in the straightest direction, requires fewer markers, and will be easy to read during later inspections.

Representatives of both activities attend the first map review. Set-net users draw their usual net positions at different tides on transparent sheets; mobile operators mark their usual fishing areas. When the sheets are overlaid, Cheng Fang sees that the original line would exclude some customary net positions from the area available to set nets. If those operations moved into adjacent water outside the small zoning trial, they could overlap with mobile fishing already there. Separation inside the trial might simply displace the problem beyond it.

The two sides do not share a single preferred answer either. The set-net side wants to retain a section it has long used, while the mobile-operation side worries that doing so would narrow the water available to them. Under the original process, Cheng Fang could simply listen to both sides and let the management office choose a compromise afterward. But the authorization for this trial already allows the management office to determine this particular boundary jointly with representatives of both affected groups. Cheng Fang therefore lays out three alternative lines, and management staff and representatives from both sides jointly eliminate the unacceptable versions and settle on one together.

The office will formally issue the jointly chosen boundary, consolidate the records, and arrange the review. Representatives of both activities divide up the work of recording overlap, unusual events, and changes in their own operating locations, then interpreting those records together. The office has to redo the trial charts, and several representatives stay to check recording methods on an afternoon they had planned to leave port. The clock passes the original finishing time while the three alternative charts still lie on the table.

On Friday afternoon, the new chart is spread across the wooden table in the dockside warehouse. Cheng Fang lifts the original straight-line draft and compares it with the new one for a few seconds, then rolls the old version up and puts it into the map tube. A half-used pencil still rests across the new boundary, with a small blank area beside it left for the next review.
articles.overall: This article illustrates a cooperative form of co-management: within a defined authorization, resource users and the public authority choose a management arrangement jointly and take on corresponding recording and review responsibilities, so participation goes beyond supplying comments.
explanationParagraphs: This example limits the shared decision to one narrow management matter: a temporary operating boundary between set-net and mobile fishing operations. The management office originally held the decision authority, but the existing authorization allows this boundary to be determined jointly with representatives of both affected groups. Their information therefore does more than enter the record; it actually changes the available options and the final boundary.

This story selects a cooperative form involving a joint decision. Real co-management spans different consultative, cooperative, and delegated arrangements; this example is not the only valid template.

Co-management does not require every party to hold exactly equal power, nor does it mean that the public authority withdraws. The management office still carries responsibility for formal issuance, consolidation, and review, while resource users carry the agreed responsibilities for observation, recording, and interpretation. A single joint decision also cannot demonstrate that operational conflict, resource condition, or ecological outcomes have already improved; actual records and subsequent review are still needed.

module.intro: This example focuses on a cooperative form involving a joint decision: share a choice within a defined authorization and align follow-up duties with it. Other co-management forms distribute authority and responsibility differently.
module.diagramTitle: Why Does Providing Fishing-Use Data Still Not Automatically Mean Co-Management?
diagramSteps: The management office first defines the trial task narrowly: only the temporary operating boundary between set-net and mobile fishing operations is being decided
Representatives of both affected fishing activities provide their actual use locations, revealing that the original straight-line option could create new overlap
Under the existing authorization, the management office does not decide alone but shares the choice among alternative boundaries with representatives of both groups
After the final boundary is selected, the management office retains formal issuance and record-consolidation duties, while both groups take on agreed recording and explanation responsibilities
At the scheduled review, all parties use the jointly collected and interpreted information to reconsider whether the boundary should be maintained or adjusted
diagramStepNotes: The management object must be specific. This example concerns two fishing-operation arrangements, not navigation rights, quotas, or the entire fisheries governance system.

Local knowledge suggests the original zoning could displace activity into adjacent water; actual records are still needed to test that possibility. Collecting comments and data alone does not establish the joint decision authority illustrated here.
Shared authority does not have to be equal. The key point is that resource users genuinely influence the decision within the authorized scope rather than merely hearing the result.
Power and responsibility should correspond: parties that participate in the choice should also take on implementation, recording, or review responsibilities appropriate to that scope.
One jointly chosen arrangement is only a governance mechanism; the meeting or the new boundary alone cannot demonstrate that conflict, catches, or ecological conditions have improved.
mapping: Three alternative boundaries → management options that can genuinely be decided jointly within the authorized scope.
Set-net and mobile-operation representatives → the two groups of resource users directly affected by the boundary.
Actual operating locations drawn on transparent sheets → local-use knowledge entering the management decision as evidence.
Formal issuance and consolidation by the management office → responsibilities that remain with the public authority.
The next joint review → a continuing chain linking decision, implementation, recording, and evaluation.
module.boundary: This article shows only one local co-management step within an existing authorization and does not describe actual legal powers, quotas, or licensing arrangements in any jurisdiction. Shared authority need not be equal, and the capacities and responsibilities of different parties may differ; attending a meeting, supplying data, or hearing a report does not automatically constitute co-management. Local knowledge and survey information both require scrutiny, and no single representative can automatically stand for every affected user. One joint decision does not guarantee improvement in conflict, catch, or ecological condition, and the operating boundary in this story is not a navigation prohibition.
module.reflection: If the management office still asked both groups to collect data and attend every discussion but required the final boundary to be chosen by the office alone after the meeting, what essential element would be missing compared with the arrangement in this story?

references.citation: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. (n.d.). Report of the Expert Consultation on Small-Scale Fisheries Management in Sub-Saharan Africa, Accra, Ghana, 12–14 December 2001: Co-management.
references.use: Supports that resource users, public authorities, and other parties can share management responsibilities and authority within a defined scope, and that co-management can take multiple forms without meaning that government abandons responsibility. This article borrows only that general governance relationship, does not generalize regional experience to all fisheries, provides no real legal authority or quota arrangement, and does not guarantee resource recovery from a single joint decision.

references.citation: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. (n.d.). Guidelines for designing data collection and sharing systems for co-managed fisheries. Part 2: Technical guidelines. Section 2: The information needs of co-managers.
references.use: Supports that roles in co-management, data collection and interpretation, implementation of decisions, and evaluation responsibilities should be aligned, and that sharing arrangements vary with partners and the scale of the problem rather than following a fixed proportion. This article shows only one authorized boundary decision and explicitly does not treat helping collect data as equivalent to holding complete management authority.

articles.summaryZh: 第一次家庭开放日前，顾遥把农场路线排得很紧凑。一场雨和一次共同试走，让最方便的院角有了新的问题。
storyParagraphsZh: 社区农场第一次办家庭开放日，顾遥负责把动物接触区、休息桌和小菜园串成一条路线。她最初只想解决一个现实问题：场地不大，带孩子的家庭越少绕路越好。于是她把最热闹的几处都安排在主棚旁边，工作人员站在一个位置就能照看到大半个院子。
试走时，动物照护员先指出，连续排队会占掉动物平时可以退到后侧安静区域的空间。当天傍晚又下了一场雨，环境维护人员沿着院子的低处看了一遍，发现棚边的水会流过原定休息区，再汇向菜园边的土带。他没有说水里一定有什么，只提醒顾遥：如果开放日人多，这里既是人停留的地方，也是场地水流经过的地方。
第二天，负责访客健康安排的人和照护、环境维护人员一起重走路线。他们在同一张图上标出洗手与接触动物的位置、动物能退开的空间，以及水流经过的地方。环境人员又圈住土带和菜园：接水的土壤和植物本身也要了解，不能只看水是否绕开游客。顾遥看着几种需要挤在同一个院角，发现手里的资料还不足以决定这里在忙碌或降雨之后怎样开放。
顾遥把主棚旁的低处休息区和相邻菜园暂时留在首日开放范围之外，动物接触安排也移开连续排队的位置，等不同专业把需要进一步判断的信息补齐后再决定是否扩大开放。这样一来，家庭少了一个参观点，休息位置更远，当天能接待的人数也必须下调。
开放当天上午，孩子们从新入口进来，主棚旁那条原本画满箭头的地面没有摆桌子。顾遥走过去，把围住低处区域的最后一根绳带扣好，又把原路线图折成四折塞进外套口袋。她从口袋里取出一张小小的“暂缓”标签，贴在绳带旁的牌子上。
articles.overallZh: 这篇在讲：当同一个场地决定同时影响人的接触活动、动物使用空间和环境条件时，只优化其中一个方向可能把负担转移给另外两个方向，因此需要不同专业把信息放在同一判断中共同取舍。
explanationParagraphsZh: 本例中的关键不是三个人分别提供三份意见，而是不同专业的信息实际改变了同一个开放决定。公共健康关注访客停留和动物接触，动物照护关注动物能否退开及其使用空间，环境人员关注雨后水流和低处土带；这些关系在同一小块场地交汇，因此只按游客便利优化路线不足以覆盖全部健康相关条件。
环境端也不是单纯替人寻找暴露通道，还包括接水土壤和植物本身的状态；本例没有声称这些地方已经受污染。
这种共同判断不表示人、动物和环境一定共享同一个病原，也不能从一次降雨、位置接近或空间共现证明传播。资料不足时可以保留未知并暂缓部分开放。协作仍需尊重各专业的诊断、环境判断、权限和隐私边界，新方案也不能被当作已经证明安全。

moduleZh.intro: 把同一个场地选择同时放到人的接触、动物使用空间和环境条件中看，检查一个方向的便利是否把风险或负担转移到另一个方向。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么最方便的开放路线仍需要人、动物与环境信息一起判断
diagramSteps: 先确定原方案把动物接触、游客休息和菜园参观集中在主棚旁的同一小块区域
动物照护信息显示连续排队会占用动物平时退开的空间
环境观察显示雨后场地水流会经过原定休息区并汇向菜园边低处，但并未因此证明污染
公共健康、动物照护和环境人员把访客接触、动物使用空间与水流信息叠到同一场地判断中
由于现有信息仍不足，首日暂缓开放其中一部分区域，并保留之后根据进一步专业判断调整的可能
diagramStepNotes: 人的便利只是场地选择的一项目标，不能单独代表整体健康条件。
动物是否拥有退开和安静空间是动物健康与福利相关信息，但不能由一次行为直接诊断疾病。
水流提供环境连接关系，不代表已经检测到污染物、病原或传播。
跨专业信息需要进入同一评估和判断；评估可能支持维持原方案，也可能要求改变。本故事中，它们确实改变了开放范围。
暂缓意味着保留未知并继续判断，不等于已经证明该区域危险，也不等于其他区域获得健康安全认证。
mapping: 访客停留与动物接触位置 → 人的健康相关接触情境。
动物后侧退避空间 → 动物使用同一场地的健康与福利条件。
雨后水流、土带和菜园 → 既连接不同区域，也提醒评估接水土壤和植物本身的状态。
三类信息叠在同一张图上 → 不同专业共同修正同一个选择。
“暂缓”标签 → 资料不足时保留判断而非强行给出安全或危险结论。

articles.title: The Courtyard Corner That Waited
articles.summary: Before the farm's first family open day, Gu Yao has planned a compact route. Rain and a joint walk-through raise new questions about its most convenient corner.
storyParagraphs: The community farm is preparing its first family open day, and Gu Yao is responsible for linking the animal-contact area, rest tables, and small vegetable garden into one route. At first she wants to solve only one practical problem: the site is small, so families with children should have to make as few detours as possible. She therefore places the busiest activities beside the main shed, where staff can see most of the courtyard from one position.

During the trial walk, the animal-care worker first points out that a continuous visitor queue would occupy the space animals normally use to retreat toward the quieter rear area. That evening it rains, and the environmental-maintenance worker follows the low points of the courtyard and notices that water from beside the shed flows across the planned rest area and then toward the low soil strip beside the vegetable garden. He does not claim that the water necessarily contains anything harmful; he simply points out that during a busy open day this would be both a place where people linger and a place crossed by site runoff.

The next day, the person responsible for visitor health walks the route with the care and environmental-maintenance staff. On one map they mark handwashing and animal-contact locations, the animals' retreat space, and the water's path. The environmental worker circles the soil strip and garden: the receiving soil and plants need attention themselves, not only whether water avoids visitors. Looking at these needs crowded into one corner, Gu Yao finds that her information is still insufficient to decide how it should open under heavy use or after rain.

Gu Yao keeps the low rest area beside the main shed and the adjacent vegetable garden outside the opening-day area, and moves the animal-contact arrangement away from the location where visitors would otherwise queue continuously. Those parts can be reconsidered after the different professionals obtain the additional information they need. The trade-off is immediate: families lose one stop, the rest area is farther away, and the number of visitors that can be received that day has to be reduced.

On the morning of the open day, children enter through the new entrance, and no tables stand on the section of ground beside the main shed that had originally been covered with route arrows. Gu Yao walks over, fastens the last rope barrier around the low area, and folds the original route map into quarters before slipping it into her coat pocket. She takes a small “temporarily deferred” label from her pocket and fixes it to the sign beside the rope.
articles.overall: This article explains that when one site decision simultaneously affects human contact, animal-use space, and environmental conditions, optimizing only one of those dimensions can shift burdens onto the others, so different professional perspectives need to be brought into the same preventive judgment and trade-off.
explanationParagraphs: The key in this example is not that three people each supply separate opinions, but that information from different specialties actually changes the same opening decision. Public health focuses on where visitors stop and contact animals, animal care focuses on whether animals can withdraw and how they use the space, and environmental staff focus on post-rain water flow and the low soil strip. Because these relationships converge in the same small area, optimizing the route only for visitor convenience is not enough to cover all health-related conditions.

The environmental perspective also concerns the receiving soil and plants themselves, rather than treating the environment only as an exposure route to people. The example does not establish that either is contaminated.

This kind of joint judgment does not mean that humans, animals, and the environment necessarily share the same pathogen, nor can one infer transmission merely from rain, proximity, or spatial co-occurrence. When information is incomplete, uncertainty can be retained and part of the site can remain temporarily unopened. Collaboration still has to respect the diagnostic roles, environmental judgments, authority, and privacy boundaries of each profession, and a revised plan cannot be treated as proof that the site is safe.

module.intro: Evaluate the same site choice simultaneously through human contact, animal-use space, and environmental conditions, and ask whether convenience in one direction shifts risk or burden into another.
module.diagramTitle: Why Does the Most Convenient Visitor Route Still Need Human, Animal, and Environmental Information to Be Considered Together?
diagramSteps: Start with the original plan, which concentrates animal contact, visitor rest, and vegetable-garden access in the same small area beside the main shed
Animal-care information shows that continuous queuing would occupy the space animals normally use to withdraw
Environmental observation shows that post-rain runoff crosses the planned rest area and reaches the low ground beside the garden, without thereby proving contamination
Public-health, animal-care, and environmental staff combine information about visitor contact, animal-use space, and water movement in the same site decision
Because the available information remains incomplete, part of the area is deferred on the first day while the option to revise the plan after further professional judgment is kept open
diagramStepNotes: Human convenience is only one objective in the site decision and cannot by itself represent the overall health conditions.
Whether animals have access to retreat and quiet space is relevant to animal health and welfare, but one observed behavior cannot by itself diagnose disease.
Water movement provides an environmental connection between locations; it does not prove that pollutants, pathogens, or transmission are present.
Information from different specialties needs to inform the same assessment and judgment. That assessment may support retaining or changing a plan; in this story it changes the opening area.
Deferral means retaining uncertainty and continuing assessment. It does not prove that the deferred area is dangerous, nor does it certify the other areas as safe.
mapping: Visitor stopping and animal-contact locations → the human-health-related contact context.
The animals' rear retreat space → animal health and welfare conditions within the same site.
Runoff, soil strip, and garden → connections between areas and a reason to assess the receiving soil and plants themselves.
The three information layers on one map → different professional perspectives jointly modifying one decision.
The “temporarily deferred” sign → retaining uncertainty rather than forcing a conclusion of either safety or danger.
module.boundary: One Health emphasizes links among human, animal, plant, and ecosystem health, together with cross-disciplinary prevention and trade-offs, but it does not mean that problems occurring at the same time or place must come from the same pathogen. A single episode of runoff, animal contact, or spatial proximity cannot prove transmission, contamination, or disease. Collaboration does not replace medical, veterinary, or environmental diagnosis and does not alter each profession's authority, privacy, or responsibilities. This article shows only preventive joint site judgment and provides no real disinfection, sampling, animal relocation, medical, or environmental-engineering procedure, nor does it treat the revised plan as a safety certification.
module.reflection: If later assessment showed that post-rain runoff never crosses the visitor rest area, but animals still could not withdraw from crowds during peak periods, would you expect the original opening plan to be fully restored? Why or why not?

references.citation: World Health Organization. (2021, December 1). Tripartite and UNEP support OHHLEP's definition of "One Health".
references.use: Supports the interconnectedness of human, domestic and wild animal, plant, and ecosystem health, and supports cross-sector and community collaboration to balance optimization, prevention, and trade-offs. This article borrows only that relational framework, does not treat simultaneously occurring problems as evidence of a shared pathogen, and does not use collaboration as a substitute for professional diagnosis, authority, or privacy.

references.use: Supports jointly preventing health risks from a systems perspective and linking human health with animal, plant, and environmental conditions while preserving the responsibilities and expertise of different professions. This article does not present the webpage's stated 2022–2026 plan period as current policy beyond that period and does not use it to provide a real approval, medical, disease-control, or environmental-engineering plan.

articles.summaryZh: 两张接触图都是八蓝两白。季岚只有十分钟，要让听众明白为什么红片未必能走到同一个地方。
storyParagraphsZh: 兽医学院晚上有一场面向公众的短课，季岚只有十分钟。她桌上摆着两张接触图，每张各放十张动物卡：八张蓝卡代表演示中已假定具有阻断传播免疫的动物，两张白卡代表仍可能被感染的动物。投影片上只有“8/10有效免疫”，助教看完问：“那两张白卡，为什么会因为别的动物有免疫而不一样？”
季岚拿来一枚红色磁片，指着第一张图说：“先假设其中一只白卡动物感染了。”她把红片放在那张卡上；另一张白卡还没有感染。两张白卡之间有一条直接接触线，她沿线推动红片，不经过蓝卡就到了另一张白卡。
她把红片放回起点，再换到第二张图。这里仍是八蓝两白，但两个白点没有直接连线；从起点去另一白点，沿画出的线走，总会先碰到蓝点。演示规定蓝卡在这段时间里完全阻断传播，红片便停在蓝点前。另一张白卡没有因此变成蓝卡，却没有被这些画出的路径抵达。
季岚因此把原来准备收尾的百分比大字删掉，把两张图并排放到桌面中央。她多花时间重新画清每一条接触边，原本能讲的另一张疫苗历史幻灯片只好拿掉。正式上课时，她先让观众猜红片在两张图里各能走到哪里，再请他们自己沿线检查。
轮到一个孩子操作时，他先把红片从第一张图的起点白点推到另一个白点。换到第二张图，他沿着线推了一格，在第一个蓝点前停下。季岚没有替他跨过去。孩子把红片拿回起点，转头对助教说：“下一组也从这个白点开始吧。”助教点点头，把两张图重新摆齐。
articles.overallZh: 这篇在讲：群体免疫的一个核心机制是，部分动物具有能够阻断传播的有效免疫后，会切断某些传播链，从而间接减少其他易感动物被传播路径抵达的机会。总接种比例本身不足以说明每个接触群的保护情况。
explanationParagraphsZh: 两张图初始各有10个节点：8个假设完全阻断所设病原传播，另2个易感，有效免疫比例均为80%。演示从其中一个原本易感的节点引入假设感染；放上红片后，该点成为感染起点，另一个白点仍易感。
第一图的两个白点有直接边，传播路径可以继续；第二图去另一白点的所有画出路径都先遇到免疫节点。另一个白点没有自己变得免疫，受的是传播链被截断带来的间接保护。
推演假定同一时段内免疫完全且不衰减，传播只沿画出的边发生，没有其他通路。现实接种覆盖不等于有效免疫，不是每种疾病或疫苗都完全阻断感染传播，易感动物也可能聚集。80%不是通用安全阈值。

moduleZh.intro: 不要只数有多少动物具有有效免疫，还要沿接触网络追踪：假设病原从一个易感节点进入后，传播路径是否在抵达另一个易感节点前被有效免疫节点切断。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么两张图起始都是8/10有效免疫，另一个易感节点的传播机会却不同
diagramSteps: 建立两张各10节点的图，每张起始都有8个有效免疫节点和2个易感节点
在第一张图中，把一个易感节点设为假设感染起点，并沿其与另一个易感节点之间的直接边追踪传播
重置第二张图，再把对应易感节点设为假设感染起点
沿第二图所有画出的路径追踪，发现抵达另一个易感节点前都会先遇到假设完全阻断传播的免疫节点
比较两图：总有效免疫比例相同，但接触结构不同，使第二图中的另一个易感节点得到路径中断带来的间接保护
diagramStepNotes: 起始时8/10表示本教学模型中的有效免疫比例，不是现实接种覆盖率或安全阈值。
红色磁片代表演示中的假设感染起点；一旦演示开始，该起点不再同时被描述为未感染易感节点。
第二图与第一图使用相同节点数量和免疫假设，改变的是节点之间画出的接触关系。
路径停止依赖模型假定免疫节点在该固定教学时段内完全阻断所设病原，且不存在未画出的其他通路。
间接保护指另一个易感节点自身仍易感，但部分到达它的传播链被其他具有有效免疫的节点截断。
mapping: 8个蓝色节点 → 教学模型中假设具有完全传播阻断作用的有效免疫节点。
2个白色节点 → 演示开始前的两个易感节点。
红色磁片 → 将其中一个易感节点设为假设感染起点后的传播追踪标记。
第一图白点间直接边 → 不经过免疫节点即可抵达另一易感节点的传播路径。
第二图先经过蓝点的路径 → 有效免疫节点截断传播并为另一易感节点提供间接保护的机制。
moduleZh.boundary: 群体免疫不能由单一接种覆盖百分比直接判断。接种覆盖与同一时刻的有效免疫不同，疫苗也可能只减少临床症状、病原排出或部分传播，而不是完全阻止感染。接触网络、易感动物是否聚集、免疫随时间变化和疾病本身都会影响传播。本篇的10节点和80%只是纸面教学设定，不提供真实疫苗阈值、产品、剂量、程序、隔离或换栏方案；重新摆卡片也不等于现实动物管理建议。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果蓝卡只表示“较少发病”，却不保证阻断感染和传播，红片遇蓝点就停止的规则还能沿用吗？为什么？

referencesZh.citation: World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE). (2022). Terrestrial Animal Health Code, Chapter 4.18: Vaccination (10 August 2022 edition).
referencesZh.use: 支持接种覆盖与有效群体免疫的区分，以及不同疫苗对感染、症状、传播和病原排出的作用可能不同。免疫需求还与流行病学和易感动物分布有关；本篇借用一般概念，不把80%当真实阈值或提供具体兽医处置建议。

articles.title: Where Will the Red Token Go?
articles.summary: Both contact diagrams have eight blue cards and two white ones. Ji Lan has ten minutes to show her audience why a red token may travel differently on them.
storyParagraphs: The veterinary school is holding an evening class for the public, and Ji Lan has only ten minutes. Two contact diagrams sit on her table, each holding ten animal cards: eight blue cards represent animals assumed in the demonstration to have immunity that blocks transmission; two white cards represent animals that can still become infected. Her slide says only “8/10 effectively immune.” The teaching assistant asks, “Why would the other animals’ immunity make a difference to those two white cards?”

Ji Lan brings over a red token and points to the first diagram. “Suppose one of the white-card animals becomes infected.” She places the token on that card; the other white-card animal has not been infected. A direct contact line joins the two white cards. She pushes the token along it and reaches the other white card without passing a blue one.

She returns the token to the starting point and switches to the second diagram. It still has eight blue cards and two white ones, but no direct line joins the white points. Every drawn route from the starting point to the other white point meets a blue point first. The demonstration assumes that blue cards completely block transmission during this period, so the token stops before the blue point. The other white card has not turned blue, but these drawn paths do not reach it.

Ji Lan therefore removes the large percentage figure she had planned to use as the conclusion and places the two diagrams side by side in the centre of the table. She spends extra time redrawing every contact edge clearly, so another slide on vaccination history has to be dropped. During the actual class, she first asks the audience to guess how far the red token can travel on each diagram and then asks them to trace the lines themselves.

When it is one child's turn, he first pushes the red token from the starting white node to the other white node on the first diagram. On the second diagram, he follows the line one step and stops before the first blue node. Ji Lan does not move it across for him. The child returns the token to the starting point and turns to the teaching assistant. “Let's have the next group start from this white node too.” The assistant nods and straightens the two diagrams again.
articles.overall: This article explains one core mechanism of herd immunity: when some animals have effective immunity that interrupts transmission, they can break certain transmission chains and indirectly reduce the chance that transmission paths reach other susceptible animals. Overall vaccination coverage alone is not enough to describe protection within every contact group.
explanationParagraphs: Both diagrams initially contain 10 nodes: 8 are assumed to completely block transmission of the specified pathogen and 2 are susceptible, giving 80% effective immunity. A hypothetical infection is introduced at one initially susceptible node. Once the red token is placed, that node is the infected starting point; the other white node remains susceptible.

The white nodes in the first diagram have a direct edge, so a transmission path remains. Every drawn route to the other white node in the second diagram first encounters an immune node. That white node has not acquired immunity itself: it receives indirect protection from interruption of the transmission chain.

The model assumes complete immunity without waning during one period, transmission only along drawn edges, and no other routes. Real vaccination coverage is not the same as effective immunity, not every disease or vaccine completely blocks infection and transmission, and susceptibility can cluster. 80% is not a universal safety threshold.

module.intro: Do not only count how many animals have effective immunity. Trace the contact network instead: after a pathogen is hypothetically introduced through one susceptible node, ask whether effective immunity interrupts the transmission path before it reaches another susceptible node.
module.diagramTitle: Why Can Two Diagrams Both Start at 8/10 Effective Immunity Yet Give the Other Susceptible Node Different Transmission Opportunities?
diagramSteps: Create two 10-node diagrams, each starting with 8 effectively immune nodes and 2 susceptible nodes
In the first diagram, designate one susceptible node as the hypothetical infected starting point and trace transmission along its direct edge to the other susceptible node
Reset the second diagram and designate the corresponding susceptible node as the hypothetical infected starting point
Trace every drawn route in the second diagram and observe that each encounters an immune node assumed to completely block transmission before reaching the other susceptible node

Compare the diagrams: the total effective-immunity proportion is the same, but the contact structure differs, giving the other susceptible node in the second diagram indirect protection through interruption of transmission paths
diagramStepNotes: At the start, 8/10 represents effective immunity in this teaching model, not a real vaccination-coverage figure or safety threshold.

The red token marks the hypothetical infected starting point used in the demonstration; once the demonstration begins, that node is no longer simultaneously described as an uninfected susceptible node.
The second diagram uses the same number of nodes and the same immunity assumptions as the first; what changes is the drawn contact relationship among the nodes.
The path stops only because the model assumes that immune nodes completely block the specified pathogen during that fixed teaching period and that no unshown transmission routes exist.
Indirect protection means that the other susceptible node remains susceptible itself, but some transmission chains that could reach it are interrupted by other nodes with effective immunity.
mapping: 8 blue nodes → effectively immune nodes assumed in the teaching model to completely block transmission.
2 white nodes → the two susceptible nodes before the demonstration begins.
Red token → the transmission-tracing marker after one of the susceptible nodes is designated as the hypothetical infected starting point.
Direct edge between white nodes in the first diagram → a transmission route that can reach the other susceptible node without passing through an immune node.
Routes in the second diagram that first meet blue nodes → the mechanism by which effectively immune nodes interrupt transmission and provide indirect protection to the other susceptible node.
module.boundary: Herd immunity cannot be determined directly from a single vaccination-coverage percentage. Vaccination coverage differs from effective immunity at a particular moment, and some vaccines may reduce clinical disease, pathogen shedding, or some transmission without completely preventing infection. Contact networks, clustering of susceptible animals, changes in immunity over time, and the disease itself all affect transmission. The 10-node structure and 80% figure in this article are only paper-model assumptions and provide no real vaccine threshold, product, dose, schedule, isolation procedure, or animal-group rearrangement plan. Rearranging cards is not equivalent to a real animal-management recommendation.
module.reflection: If blue cards mean only “less clinical illness” without guaranteeing that infection and transmission are blocked, can the rule that stops the red token at a blue point still be used? Why?

references.citation: World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE). (2022). Terrestrial Animal Health Code, Chapter 4.18: Vaccination (10 August 2022 edition).
references.use: Supports distinguishing vaccination coverage from effective population immunity and recognizing that vaccines can differ in their effects on infection, symptoms, transmission and shedding. Immunity requirements also depend on epidemiology and susceptible-animal distribution. This article borrows general concepts, not a real 80% threshold or veterinary control plan.

articles.summaryZh: 兔舍吃喝稳定，干净又安静，苏岑已排好全天探访。照护员却请她多看几次走廊有人经过时的情形。
storyParagraphsZh: 动物收容中心准备重新开放公众探访，苏岑负责安排兔舍一天开放多久。饲料、饮水和环境记录都很稳定，近期也没有发现明显健康异常；从门口看进去，兔舍干净又安静。她原本已经把整天的开放时段排进周末预约系统。
照护员却提醒她，最近几次有人从走廊经过时，有几只兔会长时间停住。苏岑没有把这个动作马上解释成害怕，也没有反过来把“安静”当成没问题。接下来几天，她在不同时间经过兔舍：有的兔在有人靠近时停住，走廊安静后才重新探索；有的会退到遮蔽处，之后再出来；也有兔在同样时段继续休息，没有出现前两种变化。
这些差别让她重新看那张“条件都不错”的清单。吃得够、喝得到、环境整洁、近期没发现明显疾病都很重要，但这些信息还需要和动物如何使用空间、能否选择接近或退开、是否探索和正常休息等观察放在一起。兽医也提醒，若出现健康或疼痛疑问，仍要按专业方式继续评估，不能拿行为观察替代健康判断。
苏岑把全天开放改成几个分开的短时段，中间保留没有访客的空档，并减少同一时间进入走廊的人数。这样做意味着周末能预约的人变少，志愿者原本连续排好的讲解班次也要拆开，但动物仍保留了更多退开、休息和在安静时段探索的机会。
第一场探访结束后，走廊门合上了。前排一只兔过了一会儿从遮蔽处出来，另一只仍趴在原地。苏岑没有因为前一只出来就去改下一场安排，只在观察卡上记下时间，又把笔插回门边的小夹槽里。门外的新时段表已经提前贴好，下一场仍按原定的间隔开始。
articles.overallZh: 这篇在讲：判断动物福利不能只看吃得够、环境整洁或没有明显疾病，还需要结合行为互动等多类证据，谨慎推断动物可能经历的负面与积极精神状态。
explanationParagraphsZh: 五域模型先从四类可观察证据入手：营养、物理环境、健康以及行为互动。它们不是四个互不相干的分数，而是共同提供线索，用来谨慎推断动物可能经历的第五类精神状态。
例如，充足饮食和整洁环境重要，但仍需同时关注健康问题，以及动物与环境、同伴和人互动时是否有退开、探索、休息或其他行为机会。
第五域不是独立再测一次的量尺，也不能把五项简单相加得到福利总分。一次安静、一次接近、一次退开或一次探索都不足以直接读出动物内心；安静可能与休息、害怕、抑制或身体不适等多种情况相符。评估既要减少可能的负面体验，也要注意是否存在积极体验的机会，而健康或疼痛疑问仍需要相应专业评估。

moduleZh.intro: 先从营养、环境、健康和行为互动收集不同类型的证据，再把它们合在一起谨慎判断动物可能经历怎样的精神状态。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么兔舍干净、吃喝正常、没有明显疾病，仍不足以说明整体体验良好
diagramSteps: 查看营养相关证据，例如采食与饮水是否保持稳定
查看物理环境证据，例如空间、遮蔽、安静条件和环境状态
查看健康证据，并在出现健康或疼痛疑问时继续由专业人员评估
查看行为互动证据，包括动物是否能选择接近、退开、探索、休息以及对访客出现的不同反应
把前四类证据综合起来，谨慎推断可能的负面和积极精神体验，而不是把它们加成一个总分
diagramStepNotes: 营养充足是重要条件，但不能单独代表整体福利。
物理环境不仅是干净与否，也包括动物实际能够使用和选择的空间条件。
行为变化不能替代健康评估；身体不适也可能改变安静、活动或互动方式。
一次停住、接近或退开都可能有多种解释，因此需要结合情境和连续观察。
第五域是由前四类证据支持的谨慎精神状态推断，不是第五个独立可相加分数；同时应考虑减少负面体验与提供积极体验机会。
mapping: 稳定的采食和饮水 → 营养领域的证据。
整洁兔舍、遮蔽处和安静空档 → 物理环境领域的证据。
近期健康记录与必要时继续评估 → 健康领域的证据。
停住、退开、探索、休息和与访客的互动 → 行为互动领域的证据。
不贴情绪标签而继续综合观察 → 用前四域证据谨慎推断精神状态。
moduleZh.boundary: 动物福利五域模型不是五个独立项目简单加分，也不是通过某一个动作直接读取动物精神状态。安静、接近、退开、探索或休息都可能有多种解释，需要结合营养、物理环境、健康和行为互动等证据以及时间情境综合判断。健康或疼痛问题不能被行为观察跳过，精神状态推断也不是诊断。本篇不提供治疗、饲养处方或通用评分阈值，只展示如何从多类证据同时考虑潜在负面体验与积极体验机会。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果兔舍的访客全部取消后，一只兔仍持续减少探索，而采食和健康记录也开始变化，你还会把原先的访客安排当成主要解释吗？接下来哪些证据的重要性会改变？

referencesZh.use: 支持2020版五域模型以前四类证据领域——营养、物理环境、健康和行为互动——共同支持对第五精神状态的谨慎推断，并支持福利评估既关注减少负面体验，也关注积极体验机会以及动物与环境、其他动物和人的互动；本篇不把五域简单相加成总分，不从单一行为直接读心，也不以行为观察替代健康或疼痛评估。

referencesZh.use: 支持以前四领域的条件与互动作为结构化证据入口，综合推断第五精神状态，并说明该框架可用于不同物种的福利思考；本篇保留网页未核出版日期为n.d.，不把网站图示或开发内容当作新的验证量表，也不使用通用评分。

articles.title: Between Two Visits
articles.summary: The rabbit housing is clean and quiet, feeding is stable, and Su Cen has scheduled visits all day. The care worker asks her to watch more closely when people pass along the corridor.
storyParagraphs: The animal shelter is preparing to reopen public visits, and Su Cen is responsible for deciding how long the rabbit housing should be open each day. Feed, water, and environmental records are stable, and no obvious recent health abnormality has been identified; from the doorway, the housing looks clean and quiet. She has already entered a full day's visiting schedule into the weekend booking system.

The animal-care worker, however, points out that during several recent occasions when people passed along the corridor, some rabbits remained still for long periods. Su Cen does not immediately interpret that behavior as fear, nor does she treat “quiet” as proof that nothing is wrong. Over the next several days, she passes through the housing at different times: some rabbits become still when people approach and begin exploring again after the corridor becomes quiet; some retreat into covered areas and later come back out; others continue resting during the same periods without showing either of those changes.

Those differences make her reconsider the checklist that had seemed to show that “conditions are good.” Having enough food and water, a clean environment, and no obvious recent disease are all important, but this information also needs to be considered together with how the animals use the space, whether they can choose to approach or withdraw, and whether they explore and rest normally. The veterinarian also reminds her that if questions about health or pain arise, they still need appropriate professional assessment rather than having behavioral observations substitute for health evaluation.

Su Cen replaces full-day opening with several separate shorter visiting periods, keeps visitor-free intervals between them, and reduces the number of people entering the corridor at one time. The change means fewer weekend bookings and requires the volunteers' previously continuous interpretation shifts to be split apart, but it also preserves more opportunities for the rabbits to withdraw, rest, and explore during quiet periods.

After the first visiting period ends, the corridor door closes. One rabbit near the front emerges from a covered area after a while, while another remains lying where it was. Su Cen does not change the next session because the first rabbit came out. She simply records the time on the observation card and returns the pen to the small holder beside the door. The new timetable is already posted outside, and the next group will still begin after the planned interval.
articles.overall: This article explains that animal welfare cannot be judged only from adequate feeding, a clean environment, or the absence of obvious disease. Evidence from behavior and interactions also needs to be considered alongside other domains to cautiously infer possible negative and positive mental experiences.
articles.conceptName: Five Domains model of animal welfare
explanationParagraphs: The Five Domains model begins with four categories of observable evidence: nutrition, physical environment, health, and behavioral interactions. These are not four unrelated scores. Together they provide evidence used to cautiously infer the fifth domain, the animal's possible mental state.

Adequate food and a clean environment are important, for example, but health concerns still need attention, as do whether animals can withdraw, explore, rest, and engage with their environment, other animals, and people.

The fifth domain is not an independent extra measuring scale, and the five domains cannot simply be added together into a welfare total. One episode of stillness, approach, withdrawal, or exploration is not enough to read an animal's internal state directly. Quiet behavior may be consistent with rest, fear, suppression, physical discomfort, or other possibilities. Welfare assessment therefore considers both reducing potential negative experiences and providing opportunities for positive experiences, while health or pain concerns still require appropriate professional evaluation.

module.intro: Begin with different kinds of evidence from nutrition, environment, health, and behavioral interactions, then consider them together when cautiously inferring what kinds of mental experiences the animal may be having.
module.diagramTitle: Why Are a Clean Rabbit Area, Normal Eating and Drinking, and No Obvious Disease Still Not Enough to Show That Overall Experience Is Good?
diagramSteps: Examine nutrition-related evidence, such as whether feeding and drinking remain stable
Examine evidence from the physical environment, including space, shelter, quiet conditions, and the state of the surroundings
Examine health evidence and continue professional assessment whenever health or pain concerns arise
Examine behavioral-interaction evidence, including whether animals can choose to approach, withdraw, explore, rest, and how they respond differently to visitors
Consider the first four categories of evidence together to cautiously infer possible negative and positive mental experiences rather than adding them into a single score
diagramStepNotes: Adequate nutrition is important but cannot by itself represent overall welfare.
The physical environment concerns not only cleanliness but also the space and choices animals can actually use.
Behavioral change cannot replace health assessment; physical discomfort can also alter stillness, activity, or interaction.
A single episode of stillness, approach, or withdrawal may have several explanations and therefore needs to be interpreted with context and repeated observation.

The fifth domain is a cautious inference about mental state supported by evidence from the first four domains, not a fifth independent score that can be added to them; assessment also considers both reducing negative experiences and providing opportunities for positive ones.
mapping: Stable feeding and drinking → evidence from the nutrition domain.
Clean housing, covered retreat areas, and quiet intervals → evidence from the physical-environment domain.
Recent health records and further assessment when needed → evidence from the health domain.
Stillness, withdrawal, exploration, rest, and interactions with visitors → evidence from the behavioral-interactions domain.
Continuing integrated observation without assigning emotion labels → cautiously inferring mental state from evidence across the first four domains.
module.boundary: The Five Domains model of animal welfare is not a system in which five independent items are simply added together, nor is it a way to read an animal's mental state directly from one behavior. Stillness, approach, withdrawal, exploration, or rest can each have multiple explanations and need to be interpreted together with evidence from nutrition, physical environment, health, behavioral interactions, and the relevant time and context. Health or pain concerns cannot be skipped because behavioral observations are available, and an inference about mental state is not a diagnosis. This article provides no treatment, husbandry prescription, or universal welfare scoring threshold and only illustrates how multiple kinds of evidence can be used to consider both possible negative experiences and opportunities for positive ones.
module.reflection: If all visitors were removed but one rabbit still continued to explore less, while its feeding and health records also began to change, would you still treat the original visitor arrangement as the main explanation? Which kinds of evidence would become more important next?

references.citation: Mellor, D. J., Beausoleil, N. J., Littlewood, K. E., McLean, A. N., McGreevy, P. D., Jones, B., & Wilkins, C. (2020). The 2020 Five Domains Model: Including Human–Animal Interactions in Assessments of Animal Welfare. Animals, 10(10), 1870. https://doi.org/10.3390/ani10101870
references.use: Supports the 2020 Five Domains model in which four evidence domains—nutrition, physical environment, health, and behavioral interactions—jointly support cautious inference about the fifth domain of mental state. It also supports considering opportunities for positive experience as well as reducing negative experience, including interactions with the environment, other animals, and people. This article does not add the five domains into a simple total score, does not infer mental state directly from one behavior, and does not use behavioral observation to replace health or pain assessment.

references.use: Supports using conditions and interactions across the first four domains as a structured evidence base for inferring the fifth domain of mental state and presents the framework as an entry point for welfare assessment across species. This article preserves the website's unverified publication date as n.d., does not treat website graphics or development content as a newly validated scale, and does not use a universal scoring system.
